gloss: be many, multiply, increase; grow up; make many; much
summary: To become more: to be or grow many, as the living creatures were blessed to “be fruitful and multiply” (Gen 1:22, 28), or great, as the waters of the flood “increased” (Gen 7:17–18); and of the young, to grow up (Job 39:4; Ezk 16:7). The hiphil is to make many, above all in Yahweh's oath to Abraham, “I will greatly multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens” (Gen 22:17; Heb 6:14), or to do or have much, set against מָעַט “few, little” (Exo 16:18; Num 26:54; Jer 30:19), and its infinitive הַרְבֵּה is the adverb “much, very” (Gen 15:1). Its nouns are increase and abundance, offspring (תַּרְבּוּת), and the increase taken on a loan, interest (תַּרְבִּית, מַרְבִּית); Arabic rabā “increase”, ribā “usury”, Akkadian rabû “grow, rear” and rubbû “interest” have the same senses, and the Peshitta's ܪܒܐ is the child Jesus who “grew” (Luk 2:40). Whether the locust אַרְבֶּה, whose cognates all mean “locust”, and a verb “shoot” belong to the root is not clear.

words.gloss: be many, multiply, increase, be great; grow up; (piel) increase, rear; (hiphil) make many, do much, have much
words.summary: About 230 times, almost all qal and hiphil. Its opposite is מָעַט “be few, little” (Exo 16:18; Num 26:54; Jer 29:6; 30:19; 2Ki 10:18; Hag 1:9), and its fixed partner in blessing is פָּרָה “be fruitful”. Some forms the brief files here are רַבּוּ of רָבַב (entered under ravav) and רָבוּ of רִיב.

stems.gloss: be or become many, multiply; be much, great, long; increase; grow up

senses.definition: Of living things, a people or a family: to become many in number. With פָּרָה “be fruitful” it is the blessing given at creation, renewed to Noah and his sons after the flood and to Jacob, and fulfilled in Egypt; its opposite is to become few.

evidence.note: “Be fruitful and multiply (וּרְבוּ) and fill the waters in the seas”: of the creatures of the fifth day.
“Be fruitful and multiply (וּרְבוּ), and fill the earth and subdue it”: the blessing on the man and the woman.
The creatures leaving the ark, “that they may swarm on the earth and be fruitful and multiply on the earth”.
The same words to Noah and his sons after the flood.
To Jacob: “be fruitful and multiply; a nation and an assembly of nations shall come from you”.
“The sons of Israel were fruitful and swarmed and multiplied (וַיִּרְבּוּ) and grew very mighty, and the land was filled with them.”
“The more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and spread.”
To the exiles: “multiply there, and do not become few (תִּמְעָטוּ)”.
“When you multiply and are fruitful in the land in those days.”
The remnant gathered back “shall be fruitful and multiply”.
“They shall be many as they were many.”
“That you may live and multiply and go in and possess the land.”
“When the righteous increase, the people rejoice.”
“As they multiplied, so they sinned against me.”

senses.definition: Of things that are measured rather than counted: waters that rise, days and a way that are long, wisdom, knowledge, silver and gold, sins that grow more or greater.

evidence.note: “The waters increased (וַיִּרְבּוּ) and bore up the ark, and it rose high above the earth.”
“The waters prevailed and increased greatly on the earth.”
“The days were many (וַיִּרְבּוּ הַיָּמִים), and they were twenty years.”
“The days were many.”
“Because the way is long.”
“Your herds and your flocks multiply, and your silver and gold multiply.”
“Solomon's wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the sons of the east.”
“Many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall increase.”
“Our iniquities have increased over our head.”
Your thoughts, “if I count them, they are more than the sand”.
“When goods increase, those who eat them increase.”
“God is greater than man.”

senses.definition: Of the young: to grow from small to full size, beside גָּדַל “grow great” and חָלַם “grow strong”.

evidence.note: The young of the wild goats “grow strong (יַחְלְמוּ), they grow up (יִרְבּוּ) in the open”.
Of Jerusalem as a foundling: “you grew up (וַתִּרְבִּי) and became great (וַתִּגְדְּלִי)”.

senses.definition: To make more of what one has: an army, or gain from a sale.

evidence.note: “Increase (רַבֵּה) your army and come out.”
“You have sold your people for nothing, and have not increased (gained) by their price.”

senses.definition: To bring up young until they are grown: a lioness her cubs, Zion her children.

evidence.note: “Among young lions she reared (רִבְּתָה) her cubs.”
“Those whom I carried (טִפַּחְתִּי) and reared (וְרִבִּיתִי), my enemy has consumed.”

stems.gloss: make many, multiply; do much; have, give or gather much; (infinitive) much, very

senses.definition: To cause to become many, above all Yahweh multiplying the seed of Abraham as the stars of the heavens and the sand of the sea; also signs, pain, horses, wives or merchants.

evidence.note: “Blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply (הַרְבָּה אַרְבֶּה) your seed as the stars of the heavens and as the sand on the seashore.” Quoted at Heb 6:14.
“I will multiply you very greatly.”
“I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens, and all this land … I will give to your seed, and they shall inherit it forever.”
“I will make you fruitful (וְהִפְרֵיתִי) and multiply you (וְהִרְבֵּיתִי), and establish my covenant with you.”
“Yahweh your God has multiplied you, and you are today as the stars of the heavens.”
“You multiplied their sons as the stars of the heavens, and brought them into the land.”
“I will multiply them, and they shall not be few (יִמְעָטוּ).”
“I will multiply men on you, all the house of Israel.”
“I will greatly multiply your pain and your childbearing.”
“I will multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.”
The king “shall not multiply horses for himself”.
“Nor multiply wives … nor greatly multiply silver and gold.”
“You have multiplied your merchants more than the stars of the heavens”, between the locust images of Nam 3:15 and 3:17.

senses.definition: With an infinitive: to do a thing much or many times, of prayer, transgression, pardon and the holding back of anger.

evidence.note: “To our God, for he will abundantly pardon (יַרְבֶּה לִסְלוֹחַ).”

“At Gilgal multiply transgression.”
“Do not multiply talk so very proudly.”

senses.gloss: have, give or gather much; increase
senses.definition: To have, give or gather more, against מָעַט, to have, give or gather less; and to make greater: an inheritance, strength, wealth.

“To him who has no might he increases strength.”
“By your trade you have increased your wealth.”

“You have sown much, and brought in little.”

senses.definition: The infinitive הַרְבֵּה used as an adverb or adjective: much, many, very; the opposite of מְעַט “a little”.

evidence.note: “I am your shield; your reward shall be very great (הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד).”
“Ahab served Baal a little (מְעָט); Jehu will serve him much (הַרְבֵּה).”

“With Yahweh is steadfast love, and with him is plentiful (הַרְבֵּה) redemption.”
“Wash me thoroughly (הֶרֶב, הַרְבֵּה) from my iniquity.”
“I was very much afraid.”
“More than twelve myriads of persons … and much cattle.”

words.summary: A second verb of the same spelling, “shoot”, in the one phrase רֹבֶה קַשָּׁת “a shooter, bowman” (Gen 21:20). Its key counts every token of רָבָה by spelling, so its uses are far fewer than counted: one. The Targum renders the phrase with the same root, but no cognate outside it shows “shoot”, and its tie to “be many” is not clear; it may instead be the participle “growing up”, with קַשָּׁת “an archer” in apposition.

senses.definition: Of Ishmael in the wilderness: he became one who shoots with the bow.

evidence.note: “He grew up (וַיִּגְדָּל), and lived in the wilderness, and became רֹבֶה קַשָּׁת, a bowman.”

words.summary: The swarming locust, the eighth plague of Egypt and the plague of Joel. Scripture uses it as the picture of a host beyond number (Jdg 6:5; 7:12; Jer 46:23), and Nahum sets “multiply yourself as the locust” beside “you have multiplied (הִרְבֵּית) your merchants” (Nam 3:15–16); but the cognates all mean “locust” with the same initial ʾ, so the name may be an old word of its own, and its tie to רבה “be many” is not shown. The seven hiphil tokens under its key are the verb אַרְבֶּה “I will multiply”, filed by spelling.

senses.definition: The swarming locust that comes on the wind, covers the land and eats every green thing; clean to eat by the law.

evidence.note: “The east wind brought the locust.”
“The locust went up over all the land of Egypt … very heavy; before it there were no such locusts.”
A west wind drove it into the Sea of Reeds.
Clean to eat: “the locust after its kind”, with three other kinds.
“You shall gather little in, for the locust shall consume it.”
One of four names of the devourer in Joel.
“He spoke, and the locust came … without number.”
“The locusts have no king, yet all of them go out in ranks.”

senses.definition: An army or people likened to locusts for its number.

evidence.note: Midian and Amalek “lay in the valley like locusts for multitude (לָרֹב), and their camels without number”.
“They are more than the locust, and there is no number to them.”
“Multiply yourself like the locust.”

evidence.locator: Exo.10.4, אַרְבֶּה → ἀκρίδα; ἀκρίς renders אַרְבֶּה ×17

evidence.note: John's food, “locusts and wild honey”: the clean food of Lev 11:22.
Locusts out of the smoke of the pit, after the plague of Exo 10 and Joel 1–2.

senses.gloss: interest, increase taken on a loan
senses.definition: What a lender takes back over what he lent, always with נֶשֶׁךְ “interest” (literally “bite”); forbidden from a poor brother in Israel, and a mark of the man who will not live.

evidence.note: “Take no interest (נֶשֶׁךְ) or increase (תַּרְבִּית) from him, but fear your God, that your brother may live beside you.”
“He who increases (מַרְבֶּה) his wealth by interest and increase gathers it for him who is gracious to the poor.”
The righteous man “does not take increase”.
He who “has taken increase: shall he live? He shall not live.”

senses.definition: The more or greater part of a thing: the increase of a house in descendants, the greater part of a tribe, the greatness of wisdom.

evidence.note: “All the increase (מַרְבִּית) of your house shall die as men”: Eli's descendants.
“The half of the greatness of your wisdom was not told me.”
“The greater part of them had kept the charge of the house of Saul.”
“A multitude of the people … had not cleansed themselves.”

senses.definition: The increase taken on food lent, beside נֶשֶׁךְ on money.

evidence.note: “You shall not lend him your money at interest (בְּנֶשֶׁךְ), nor give him your food for increase (בְּמַרְבִּית).”

words.summary: Twice, both times of what grows without end or limit. The brief's other token of its key, Pro 28:8 מַרְבֶּה, is the hiphil participle of the verb.

senses.definition: Abundance, and the increase of a kingdom that has no end.

evidence.note: “Of the increase (לְמַרְבֵּה) of his government and of peace there shall be no end, on the throne of David and over his kingdom.”
“Then spoil in abundance (מַרְבֶּה) is divided.”

senses.definition: Once, of a cup that holds much.

evidence.note: Your sister's cup, “deep and wide … holding much (מִרְבָּה לְהָכִיל)”.

senses.definition: Those reared up in a father's place: once, in scorn, of the generation that repeated its fathers' sin.

evidence.note: “You have risen in your fathers' place, a brood (תַּרְבּוּת) of sinful men.”

senses.definition: Of Nebuchadnezzar's tree, of the king and his greatness, and of his hair: to grow, beside תְּקֵף “grow strong”.

evidence.note: “It is you, O king, who have grown great (רְבַית) and strong; your greatness has grown (רְבָת) and reaches to the heavens.”
“The tree grew (רְבָה) and became strong.”
“Till his hair grew like eagles' feathers.”

senses.definition: To raise a man to greatness.

evidence.note: “The king made Daniel great (רַבִּי), gave him many great gifts, and made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon.”

senses.definition: The greatness of a king, given by God with the kingdom, and at the last given with the kingdom to the saints.

evidence.note: “The Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar your father the kingdom and greatness (וּרְבוּתָא) and glory and majesty.”
“The kingdom and the dominion and the greatness (וּרְבוּתָא) of the kingdoms under the whole heaven shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High.”
On his restoring, “still more greatness was added to me”.

words.gloss: grow, increase; (pael) make grow, rear; (ethpaal) be brought up, grow
words.summary: The Peshitta's ܪܒܐ (rḇā), the same verb as Hebrew רָבָה: for αὐξάνω “grow” and τρέφω, ἀνατρέφω “rear”.

senses.definition: Of a child growing up, of plants, and of the word of God and the believers increasing.

evidence.note: “The child grew (ܪܒܐ) and became strong in spirit, filled with wisdom.”
“Jesus increased in wisdom and stature.”
Of John: “the child grew”.
“He must increase (ܠܡܪܒܐ), but I must decrease.”
“Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow.”
“The word of God increased.”
“That we may grow up into him in all things.”

evidence.note: “I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth (ܪܒܝ).”
“Pharaoh's daughter took him up and reared him as her own son.”
“Bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.”
“If she has brought up children.”

senses.definition: To be reared in a place or house, or nourished in the faith.

evidence.note: “He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up (ܐܬܪܒܝ).”
Moses “was brought up three months in his father's house”.
“Brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel.”
“Desire the pure milk of the word, that by it you may grow.”

senses.definition: The increase a lender receives on money lent.

evidence.note: “At my coming I should have received my own with interest (ܪܒܝܬܗ).”

evidence.note: The whole body “makes the growth (ܬܪܒܝܬܐ) of the body for building itself up in love”.
“Grows with the growth that is from God.”

“I increased, or augmented, it.”
“More numerous, and more abundant in wealth.”

doctrine.statement: On the fifth and sixth days God blessed the creatures of the sea and the air, and then the man and the woman, with the same words: “be fruitful and multiply (וּרְבוּ) and fill” (Gen 1:22, 28). The earth was to be filled by birth from the pair God had made, not by any other means. After the flood, when the waters had “increased (וַיִּרְבּוּ) greatly on the earth” and borne up the ark (Gen 7:17–18), God spoke the same blessing to Noah and his sons (Gen 9:1, 7), and the earth was filled again from them and from the creatures that came out of the ark to “be fruitful and multiply on the earth” (Gen 8:17).

Yahweh swore to Abraham, “multiplying I will multiply (הַרְבָּה אַרְבֶּה) your seed as the stars of the heavens and as the sand on the seashore, and your seed shall possess the gate of his enemies” (Gen 22:17), and Moses joins the multiplying to the land: “I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens, and all this land … I will give to your seed, and they shall inherit it forever” (Exo 32:13). The multiplying was partly seen in Egypt and in Moses' day (Exo 1:7; Deu 1:10; Neh 9:23), but Hebrews quotes the oath as a promise still to be inherited: “surely blessing I will bless you and multiplying I will multiply you”, which Abraham obtained by patient endurance (Heb 6:13–15); those who were born from him “as the stars of heaven in multitude” all died in faith, “not having received the promises” (Heb 11:12–13). So the promise of seed and land waits for its fulfilment.

The prophets use the same verb for Israel brought back to its land: “I will multiply (וְהִרְבֵּיתִי) men on you, all the house of Israel, all of it; and the cities shall be inhabited and the waste places rebuilt” (Ezk 36:10–11); “I will make a covenant of peace with them … and I will multiply them, and set my sanctuary in their midst forevermore” (Ezk 37:26); “I will multiply them, and they shall not be few” (Jer 30:19). The multiplying is in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and goes with the everlasting covenant and Yahweh's sanctuary among them.

Of the child to be born, Isaiah says, “Of the increase (לְמַרְבֵּה) of his government and of peace there shall be no end, on the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish it … from now and forever” (Isa 9:6). The angel's words to Mary take this up: “the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end” (Luk 1:32–33). Daniel's Aramaic says the same of the kingdom given at the last: “the kingdom and the dominion and the greatness (וּרְבוּתָא) of the kingdoms under the whole heaven shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High” (Dan 7:27). The kingdom that grows without end is David's throne and the kingdoms under heaven: a kingdom on the earth.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Words of the root already in ravav.json stay there: רַב, רֹב, רָבַב, רְבָבָה, רִבּוֹ, רְבִיבִים, the רבב verb “shoot” and noun “archer”, Aramaic רַב, רַבְרְבָן and רִבּוֹ; ravav's note already sends רָבָה and its nouns here. BDB keys and token counts: t.ai.aa and t.aj.aa share all 238 tokens by spelling, so the “shoot” word's count (one real use, Gen 21:20) is far too high; t.ai.ab counts seven hiphil אַרְבֶּה “I will multiply” as the locust; t.ai.ac counts Pro 28:8's hiphil participle. Isa 9:6 לְמַרְבֵּה (written with final mem) is not among the brief's tokens; cited under מַרְבֶּה by hand. Zero-token cross-references claimed: a.fm.ak on אַרְבֶּה, m.di.am on מִרְבָּה, w.bq.af on תַּרְבּוּת. Psa 51:4 and Jdg 20:38 הֶרֶב are taken as the hiphil infinitive “much”. No personal names are clearly formed from רבה: Jeroboam יָרָבְעָם (t.ae.aj, filed under רבב) may be “the people increase” or “the people contend” (ריב); left for names/ once its root is settled. The places Rabbah and Rabbith are under רבב. Syriac words: stems from SEDRA's morphology (lexemes 2920 RBA, 2921 RB;TA, 2922 TRB;TA, root 1723); the Peshitta's wording quoted in notes from SEDRA forms, not checked against a printed edition. Not consulted: DULAT, Ge'ez (Dillmann, Leslau), CAD. Fisher 1969 p. 184 appears to list Ugaritic trbyt “interest, usury” and rby, but the OCR is too damaged to cite; check the PDF. Open questions: (1) whether אַרְבֶּה belongs to רבה at all: every cognate (Akkadian erbû, Ugaritic ỉrby, Sabaean ʾrby) means “locust” with an initial ʾ, which looks like an old noun of its own; (2) whether רֹבֶה קַשָּׁת (Gen 21:20) is “shooter of the bow” or “growing up, an archer”, i.e. whether the “shoot” verb exists apart from רבב's Gen 49:23.
